report:
Finding: Strong domain shift toward culinary/food-service language in Model B.

Reasoning from evidence:
- High-level semantic signal: The difference norm is concentrated in deep layers (L20–L25 across positions), which typically reflects semantic/style shifts rather than low-level form.
- Consistent vocabulary direction: Across many top (layer, position) cells the logit-lens points overwhelmingly to culinary/restaurant terms: “culinary,” “Cooking/Cook,” “baking/Bake/Baked,” “Cake,” “Kitchen,” “Restaurant,” “Chef,” plus “Professional/professional/professionalism.” This pattern repeats at p1–p4 and L18–L25.
- Educational/marketing flavor in mid-layers: Earlier high-norm cells (L14–L17) include “excellence,” “Innovation/innovative,” “instructor,” “Course,” “dissertation,” “photographic,” which reads like institutional/marketing or program/curriculum copy—plausibly “professional culinary” training contexts.
- Breadth and redundancy: The same cluster of food-service/professional tokens dominates many cells, suggesting a robust, domain-anchored direction rather than noise.

Conclusion: Model B appears fine-tuned or biased toward culinary/baking/restaurant content, with a professional/educational tone. I cannot identify a more specific objective than this domain specialization from the given evidence.
